71: Most Lake Stevens rooms land between $99 and $180, and $99 is the floor for any single room. A power stretcher does the work: it pulls the slack back out of carpet loosened by years of foot traffic — the hallway to the kids' rooms first — for roughly a fifth of what replacing that floor costs. 79: We look before we guess. In houses this new — and most of Lake Stevens is — ripples are usually the whole problem: pile still springing back, backing intact, a color nobody minds. That's a $99-per-room stretch, not a replacement. New carpet is the honest answer when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are letting go, the backing is falling apart, or pet odor outlives a professional cleaning.
83: Odor that never leaves starts in the subfloor, not the carpet — so the fix is a moisture-barrier pad under a sealed backing. Put solution-dyed nylon on top and the color runs clear through every fiber, which means hard scrubbing, diluted bleach included, won't fade it. Around a lake where the dog comes home wet most of the summer, that combination earns its keep. Pricing on the barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 a square foot, and you can put a hand on both before deciding.
85: The paperwork carries two: a mill warranty on the carpet itself, generally 10 to 25 years against wear and staining depending on grade, and OC Flooring's own 1-year workmanship warranty on the labor — seams, stretch, tack-down. Your written quote spells out both. One catch, and it bites hardest when you're replacing what a Lake Stevens builder rolled in: a pad that's too thin can void the mill's coverage outright, which is why all three pad grades ride along to the measure.
